title: Testing electrical stimulation during early rehabilitation to manage phantom limb pain and improve walking after below-knee amputation
official: Early intervention with model-driven FES to manage post-amputation phantom limb pain and optimise gait (Early MoFit): a feasibility randomised trial
summary:
Background and study aims
People who have had a below-knee amputation may experience phantom limb pain, which is pain that feels as though it comes from the missing part of the leg. This pain can affect sleep, daily activities, walking and quality of life.

Functional electrical stimulation (FES) uses small electrical pulses applied through pads placed on the skin to activate muscles. Previous research suggests that using FES during walking may help reduce phantom limb pain and improve walking ability.

The Early MoFit study aims to find out whether FES can be used safely, comfortably and practically during the early stages of rehabilitation after below-knee amputation. The study will also explore whether FES may help reduce phantom limb pain and improve walking and quality of life.

Who can participate?
Adults aged 18–80 years who have had a below-knee amputation on one side within the past two years, have been using a prosthetic leg for less than one year, and currently experience phantom limb pain. Participants must be able to walk using their prosthetic leg, with or without a walking aid, and safely complete the study assessments.

What does the study involve?
Participants will be randomly assigned to start with either six weeks of FES-assisted walking or six weeks of walking without FES. After a six-week break, participants will switch to the other condition. Everyone will therefore experience both conditions.

During the FES period, participants will use a portable electrical stimulation device while walking for at least 20 minutes per day, where safe and comfortable. During the non-FES period, participants will continue their usual walking activities and wear a physical activity monitor.

Participants will complete a short daily pain diary and receive regular telephone calls from the research team.

Assessments will take place before treatment starts and at Weeks 6, 12 and 18. These will include questionnaires about pain and quality of life and short walking assessments using wearable movement sensors. A final telephone follow-up will take place at Week 21.

Each participant will take part for approximately 21 weeks, including the final follow-up.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Participants may experience improvements in phantom limb pain or walking ability, although these benefits cannot be guaranteed.

FES may cause temporary skin irritation, muscle soreness, fatigue or discomfort during stimulation. The research team will provide training and monitor participants' safety throughout the study.

The findings will help researchers understand whether FES is suitable for use during early rehabilitation and inform the design of a larger clinical trial.

Where is the study run from?
The study is sponsored by the University of Birmingham and will recruit participants from the West Midlands Rehabilitation Centre in Birmingham and Livewell Southwest in Plymouth, United Kingdom.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
January 2027 to September 2027.

Who is funding the study?
The study is funded by the Medical Research Council Impact Acceleration Account (MRC IAA), UK.

Who is the main contact?
Dr Ziyun Ding, University of Birmingham, z.ding@bham.ac.uk
conditions: Phantom limb pain following unilateral transtibial (below-knee) amputation during early prosthetic rehabilitation.

interventions.name: ODFS Pace XL Functional Electrical Stimulation (FES) device

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adults aged 18–80 years who are able to provide written informed consent
2. Unilateral transtibial (below-knee) amputation within the past two years
3. Fitted with and using a prosthesis for less than one year
4. Current phantom limb pain with a severity of at least 3/10 on a numerical rating scale (NRS)
5. Able to walk with a prosthesis, with or without an additional walking aid
6. Able to safely complete the study walking assessments, as judged by the clinical team
7. Willing and able to comply with study procedures, including use of the FES device or activity monitor, daily pain diary, study visits, and telephone reviews
Exclusion criteria:
1. Contraindications to functional electrical stimulation (FES), including cardiac pacemakers, implanted defibrillators, other implanted electronic devices, uncontrolled epilepsy, or other conditions considered unsuitable for FES by the clinical team
2. Pregnancy, planned pregnancy during the study, or current breastfeeding
3. Skin conditions, wounds, infections, marked skin sensitivity, or other local issues preventing safe electrode placement on the residual limb
4. Significant medical, neurological, cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, or other conditions that may affect safe participation
5. Inability to safely complete the study walking assessments using the usual prosthesis and walking aid, where required
6. Severe cognitive impairment or other conditions affecting the ability to provide informed consent or follow study instructions
7. Insufficient English language ability to provide informed consent and complete study procedures
8. Current participation in another interventional research study that may affect the study outcomes
9. Any other condition that, in the opinion of the clinical team, makes participation unsafe or inappropriate
